## Why `Clause-②: no`, with the control

The whole surface is `scripts/` — `scripts/__tests__/spec-symbol-ledger-plugin-detail-7265.test.ts` and, if the repair reaches it, `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs`. Under `objectstack-ai/objectstack#18885`'s ruling (2026-09-18T08:10Z, comment `5727163801`, maintainer-approved) the clause-② content limb is the PROTOCOL's public surface — spec schemas' accept set, `packages/types/**` with its schema corpus, and published `skills/**`. Path control on the surface this card names: `packages/types/` **0**, `packages/spec/` **0**, `skills/` **0**. Nothing published moves; a test gets stricter. ⛔ No carrier hung, and ⛔ none is owed.

## Re-derived on the tree before dispatch, ⛔ not adopted from the card

`main` = `6778809f5bba2d3463db49386b50dffbbe44acc8`. The card's own provenance line warns that line numbers are stale by default, so both anchors were re-read:

| what | where, today |
|:--|:--|
| the pin | `spec-symbol-ledger-plugin-detail-7265.test.ts:279` (the `it(…)`), `:283` (the regex `/^const DEBT_ISSUE = \d+;$/m`) |
| the pin's stated purpose | `:281`–`:282`, verbatim: deleting the anchor "would silently turn the stale-entry message's tail off (it is written behind a `DEBT_ISSUE ?` guard)" |
| the declaration | `check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs:889` — `const DEBT_ISSUE = 7265;` |
| the guard the pin exists to protect | `:2284` — ``${DEBT_ISSUE ? `, and objectui#${DEBT_ISSUE} can be ended once the ledger is empty` : ""}.`` |

Both hold. The card's truth table is the tree's.

## Two things the card does NOT carry, found in the same read

⭐ **`LEDGER_ANCHORS` already exists** at `check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs:1254`–`:1279` — an exported table registering `DEBT`/`DEBT_ISSUE` and `CLAIM_DEBT`/`CLAIM_DEBT_ISSUE` with their issue numbers and `state`, added because objectui#9537's ruling "keeps the anchor and buys the detection instead". Its own coverage pin lives in `spec-symbol-ledger-anchor-liveness-9537.test.ts`. The card was filed before that landed and its Ask does not mention it. This does not change the card's ask, but it changes what a good repair looks like, and the dispatch order says so rather than letting the dev rediscover it mid-flight.

⚠️ **The twin has the same gap and less cover.** `CLAIM_DEBT_ISSUE` is declared at `:1186` and guarded identically at `:2340`. The pin file touches it exactly **once** (`:356`), and that assertion is about the message SHAPE, not about the anchor being declared at all — so `CLAIM_DEBT_ISSUE` has no anchor pin to tighten, it has none to begin with. ⛔ Out of scope for this card and NOT folded into it: the gate's own note at `:878`–`:888` records `CLAIM_DEBT_ISSUE`'s exclusion as deliberate, and objectui#9537 re-affirmed it BY NAME. ⚠️ That exclusion is about RE-ANCHORING (an anchor pointing at a closed card), which is a different question from falsiness — so the gap is real and is being filed as its own card, per 「明确放过的东西必须有自己的载体」, which is the very shape this card is an instance of.

## Dispatching now

⛔ Not claiming on this comment: the order goes to a `mode:subagent` dev on the branch above, and the seat re-reads CI and mergeability at the landing flip rather than inheriting any reading taken here.

## ACCEPT — in-seat, at the default tier

`domain:ui` execution seat, `session_012EpHzwH4wTy5sd7ibkD2yq`, 2026-09-18T13:36Z. PR objectui#9888, head `0f0288493`. ⛔ Not landing on this comment: I re-read CI and mergeability at the flip rather than inheriting any reading here.

**Clause-②: no, and no carrier is owed.** Two files, both under `scripts/`. Path control on the PR's own file list: `packages/types/` **0**, `packages/spec/` **0**, `skills/` **0**, and files outside `scripts/` + `.changeset/` **0**. Under `objectstack-ai/objectstack#18885`'s ruling (2026-09-18T08:10Z) this is an ordinary lane card; ⛔ no contract review and ⛔ no tier were spent.

## The crux, measured in this seat — ⛔ not adopted from the report

The whole card turns on one regex, so I ran it myself over every leg that matters. Counting rule: each candidate declaration string, tested against the OLD pattern and the NEW one, beside what the gate's `DEBT_ISSUE ?` guard would actually do with that value.

| declaration | OLD `\d+` | NEW `[1-9]\d*` | truthy | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `const DEBT_ISSUE = 7265;` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | the tree today — green stays green |
| `const DEBT_ISSUE = 0;` | ✅ **passes** | ❌ **reds** | ❌ | ⭐ the defect, closed |
| `const DEBT_ISSUE = null;` | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | the control leg, preserved |
| `const DEBT_ISSUE = 10;` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ⭐ a truthy value CONTAINING a zero — the obvious way to get this wrong, and it is not got wrong |
| `const DEBT_ISSUE = 1;` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | smallest truthy |

The `10` row is the one I went looking for: a lazier fix (`[^0]`, or excluding the character `0` anywhere) would have reddened a perfectly good anchor. `[1-9]\d*` constrains the FIRST digit only, so the implication "matches ⇒ truthy" is exact over decimal literals rather than approximately right.

**The comment now states the invariant it enforces AND what it does not cover.** The card's Ask required the comment to move with the regex, because the two disagreed ("still declared" vs "is a decimal number") and a reader would otherwise re-derive the wrong invariant even after the regex was tightened. The rewritten block says: declared AND truthy; fails CLOSED on `0`, on `null`, and on any expression the pin cannot evaluate; and — this is the part I checked hardest — it ⛔ declines to credit itself with the deletion leg, saying that reds through `LEDGER_ANCHORS` reading the const at module scope, not through this assertion. ⚠️ I did ⛔ not re-run that leg. I am accepting it because it is disclosed in the direction that makes the pin look WEAKER, which is the direction nobody fakes.

## The shape decision was measured, and the measurement is the right one

My order offered two shapes and told the dev to measure, not prefer. They did, and the leg that separates them is the one I would not have thought to construct: put the const at `0` while leaving a truthy literal in `LEDGER_ANCHORS`. The source-text shape reds; the runtime shape goes **green — blind**.

That is decisive and the reason generalises: the guard's operand is the module-local `const`, and the table is a SECOND binding of the same number. A pin that reads the copy is asserting something about the copy. Whether the two stay faithful to each other is a different invariant, and it already has its own pin in `spec-symbol-ledger-anchor-liveness-9537.test.ts`. ⇒ the cheaper-looking shape would have moved this pin's subject one binding away from the thing the card is about.

## The changeset is idiomatic, checked rather than assumed

Empty frontmatter, i.e. no package released. Control on `main`: of **1702** files matching `.changeset/*.md`, **537** have empty frontmatter — 31.5%, an established spelling in this repo, not an improvisation. Test-only strengthening, nothing published moves.

## Two findings carried out, ⛔ neither folded in

1. **The `export ` boundary.** `anchor-liveness-9537.test.ts`'s anchor scan admits an optional `export ` prefix; this pin's line anchoring does not. Measured in this seat: `export const DEBT_ISSUE = 7265;` fails the NEW pattern — and fails the OLD one too, so ⛔ this change does not introduce it. The two files disagree about what counts as a declared anchor, and it fails SHUT, which is the safe direction.
2. **The tree-wide framing is narrower than the card and triage stated.** With the anchor at `0` the pin file is fully green, but `anchor-liveness-9537.test.ts` reds on its recurrence-path leg. That file landed AFTER this card was filed. ⇒ the card's own claim — about THIS pin — is exact; what is bounded is a stronger claim nobody actually made. Recorded, ⛔ no separate carrier owed for it.

Both go to objectui#9883, the twin card I filed while writing this dispatch, which already owns the scan's `\d+`.

## The fence I set, and how it held

⛔ `CLAIM_DEBT_ISSUE` untouched, as ordered. ⛔ objectui#9537's shape question untouched: `DEBT_ISSUE`'s value, the `state: "closed"` field and the by-name exclusion are all unchanged. ⛔ `anchor-liveness-9537.test.ts` unmodified — my amendment mid-flight told the dev that `:101`–`:107` pins `issue: 0` as deliberate silence and ⛔ must not be "fixed", and the file is not in the diff. The two questions stayed separate: that detector answers 「is this a DEAD anchor」, this pin answers 「is the instruction still switched on」.

⇒ **ACCEPT.** Landing when CI converges.
